page.layout: One page of text in two columns, with a running head at top. Below the text, a rule separates the upper section from the lower; the main text runs in a single column of paragraphs and syllogisms. No marginal notes. Catchword "Quid" at the lower right.

main_text.p: affirmata propria : ut, Quidam homo non est philosophus. Argumentum tertium: ut Therfites.
main_text.l: Ergo quidam homo non est philosophus.
main_text.head: Quid est secunda Figura?
main_text.p: EST, ubi argumentum tertium in Propositione Quaestionis consequente partem, in Assumptione antecedentem partem semper sequitur, & in Propositione, aut Assumptione negatur. Secunda Figura habet sex modos.
main_text.head: Quid est Syllogismus in Cesare primo modo?
main_text.p: Cujus propositio est negata, & omnes partes sunt generales: ut, Fideles non damnabuntur. Argumentum tertium: quia esuriunt & sitiunt justitiam.
main_text.l: Qui damnabūtur nō esuriunt, neqį sitiunt justitiā.
main_text.head: Quid est Syllogismus in Camestres secundo modo?
main_text.p: Cujus propositio est tantùm affirmata, & omnes partes generales: ut, Veri Christiani dissolutè non vivunt. Argumentum tertium: quia non sunt infideles.
main_text.l: At veri Christiani non sunt infideles.
Ergo veri Christiani dissolutè non vivunt.

page.notes: Printing errors left as printed: "Propositione Quaestionis consequente partem" and "Cujus propositio est negata" are as set. The catchword "Quid" is written both in the bottom margin and as the final element; it appears once at the foot of the page. Show-through from the reverse side and a crease running diagonally across the page were ignored. Some letters in the syllogisms are damaged by the crease ("Therfit:s", "ergo c_uidam"); these were read from context as "Therfites" and "Quidam". The word "Quid" at lower right is the catchword.
